newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -FTSE TO DROP TO AROUND 5,000-5,025.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -FTSE TO DROP TO AROUND 5,000-5,025.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index will lose its grip on the 5,075 level and drop to around 5,000-5,025 region on Wednesday with shares of banks and pharmaceuticals coming under pressure, technical analysts said.
No sooner than fighting its way back up on Tuesday, the market will be forced to beat a retreat after a collapse on Wall Street on Tuesday night, they added.
By 0729 GMT, the FTSE was indicated down 21.3 at 5,045.5.
As is usually the case whenever there is a sharp fall on Wall Street, UK shares will be marked down initially in order to fend off some selling pressure.
Just how successful this manoeuvre will be depends very much on wholesale inflation data from the U.S. due at 1230 GMT.

There is likely to be cautious trading ahead of the producer prices data for July where consensus forecast is for a month-on-month rise of 0.1 percent. Even excluding the volatile food and energy component, the rise is forecast to be 0.1 percent.

Analysts believe a rise greater than 0.2 percent will not be tolerated by the market and will have the effect of share prices falling as fears will increase that Thursday's consumer prices data will also be greater than expected so that the probability of a hike in U.S. interest rates becomes greater.
Also weighing on the market will be U.S. retail sales for July and if this is greater than 0.7 percent, share prices will weaken.
On Tuesday, the Dow Jones industrial average fell 101.27 points to 7,960.84.
